headline: Math nearly saturated while real-world agent work remains the hard frontier
outlook: Math has effectively stopped being a frontier: it closed 95% of its remaining headroom over the past year, FrontierMath crossed 90% in September, and GPT-6.1 Sol has now posted 100% on FrontierMath T4. The slowest-moving category is agents and real work, at 34% of headroom closed. GPT-6 Astra's 20.8% on the Remote Labor Index and Claude Opus 5's 31.4% on OSWorld 2 put 90% on those benchmarks out to mid-2027 and early 2028 on current trends, even though APEX-Agents jumped from 68.6% to 82.2% across three releases in late September. The bridge between the two is task length: the longest tasks models can handle now stand at 17.4 hours and have been doubling roughly every 4.2 months, which on current trends points to a full 40-hour work-week around December 2026, though the likely range runs to August 2027. Meanwhile the cheapest model scoring at least 80% on GPQA has fallen from $3.44 per million tokens to $0.055, so new capability tends to get cheap quickly, but treat all these dates loosely: past likely ranges caught the real date only 59% of the time, and Terminal-Bench and GeoBench are both running behind their fitted trends.
